'''Ramon Alexander Wyss''' (born 1 March 1952) is a Swedish theoretical [[nuclear physicist]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Borefur |first=Åsa BorefurTextÅsa |date=2022-09-29 |title=Världskonferens i "kärnkraftens vagga" lär bli återkommande |url=https://www.barometern.se/oskarshamn/varldskonferens-i-karnkraftens-vagga-lar-bli-aterkommande/ |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=Barometern-OT |language=sv}}</ref> He is a professor emeritus at the [[KTH Royal Institute of Technology]] in [[Stockholm]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=DebattredaktionenText |date=2025-02-18 |title=Sverige behöver en finsk universitetsreform |url=https://www.di.se/debatt/sverige-behover-en-finsk-universitetsreform/ |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=Dagens industri |language=sv}}</ref> He served as Vice President for International Affairs at KTH in between 2002 to 2016.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Hammar |first=Av Loth |date=2009-05-25 |title=Ramon Wyss ny vicerektor vid KTH |url=https://www.lifesciencesweden.se/article/view/471733/ramon_wyss_ny_vicerektor_vid_kth |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=Life Science Sweden}}</ref> He held professorships at [[Peking University]] and [[Shanghai Jiao Tong University]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Viewpoint: European science should be a bridge to China, not a wall {{!}} Science{{!}}Business |url=https://sciencebusiness.net/viewpoint/research-and-innovation-gap/viewpoint-european-science-should-be-bridge-china-not-wall |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=sciencebusiness.net |language=en}}</ref>

His research focuses on [[Nuclear structure|nuclear structure physics]], using simple theoretical models to elucidate complex experimental findings.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Viewpoint: Will AI help Big Tech dominate science? {{!}} Science{{!}}Business |url=https://sciencebusiness.net/viewpoint/ai/viewpoint-will-ai-help-big-tech-dominate-science |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=sciencebusiness.net |language=en}}</ref>

In 1995, he was awarded the Edlundska prize of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Edlundska priset |url=https://www.kva.se/priser/ovriga-priser/edlundska-priset/ |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Kungl. Vetenskapsakademien |language=sv-SE}}</ref>
== Early life and education ==
Ramon Wyss was born to Dieter Wyss and Ursula Wyss Daecke.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Romero |first=José Miguel L. |date=2017-06-30 |title=Nueve piezas de Wyss para la catedral |url=https://www.diariodeibiza.es/ibiza/2017/06/30/nueve-piezas-wyss-catedral-30078445.html |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=Diario de Ibiza |language=es}}</ref> He became a Swedish citizen in 1973 and earned his Teknologie doktor (PhD) in 1990, followed by a postdoc stay at the Joint Institute of [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory|Oak Ridge National Lab]] 1990-1992. He earned docent promotion in 1994 and in 2006 he was appointed professor of theoretical nuclear physics at [[KTH Royal Institute of Technology|KTH]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Prof Ramon Wyss vice president international affairs KTH Deputy |url=https://studylib.net/doc/5250956/prof-ramon-wyss-vice-president-international-affairs-kth-... |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=studylib.net |language=en}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Wyss was appointed professor of theoretical nuclear physics at KTH in 2006.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=The 499th Academic Symposium of the State Key Laboratory of Nuclear Physics and Technology Prof. Ramon Wyss (KTH the Royal Institute of Technology) |url=https://ppnp.pku.edu.cn/info/1036/2025.htm |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=Peeking University}}</ref><ref name=":5" /> 

From 2002 to 2016, Wyss served as Vice President of [[KTH Royal Institute of Technology|KTH]] in charge of international education and global partnerships.<ref name=":0" />

After retiring from KTH, Wyss has worked on interdisciplinary projects linking physics and societal challenges. With Ayşe Ataç Nyberg, he co-founded the European ArtEmis Project in 2022<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kumar |first1=Gururaj |last2=Gerl |first2=Jürgen |last3=Nyberg |first3=Ayse Atac |last4=Bäck |first4=Torbjörn |last5=DeLuca |first5=Gaetano |last6=Eleftheria |first6=Papadimitriou |last7=Guerriero |first7=Vincenzo |last8=Hůlka |first8=Jiří |last9=Karakostas |first9=Vassilis |last10=Lightfoot |first10=Alexandra |last11=Löher |first11=Bastian |last12=Nilsson |first12=Mats |last13=Sjödin |first13=Peter |last14=Tallini |first14=Marco |last15=Wyss |first15=Ramon |date=2025 |title=Earthquake precursor measurements employing a network of radon sensors |url=https://www.epj-n.org/articles/epjn/abs/2025/01/epjn20240062/epjn20240062.html |journal=EPJ Nuclear Sciences & Technologies |language=en |volume=11 |page=48 |doi=10.1051/epjn/2025045 |bibcode=2025EPJNS..11...48K |issn=2491-9292|doi-access=free |hdl=11697/270859 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>, aimed at building a sensor network to improve [[earthquake forecasting]].<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=Viewpoint: how Horizon Europe could change the face of earthquake prediction {{!}} Science{{!}}Business |url=https://sciencebusiness.net/news/viewpoint-how-horizon-europe-could-change-face-earthquake-prediction |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=sciencebusiness.net |language=en}}</ref>

He currently serves as chair of both the governing and science boards of the project. He was the interim director of the Center for New Energy Technology Oskarshamn (CNETO).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Winsell |first=Johan WinsellTextJohan |date=2023-05-01 |title=Ny internationell energikonferens planeras i Oskarshamn |url=https://www.barometern.se/oskarshamn/ny-internationell-energikonferens-planeras-i-oskarshamn/ |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=Barometern-OT |language=sv}}</ref>

He was co-chair for the International advisory board of [[Beijing Jiaotong University]] and in 2021 he was appointed to the international advisory board of [[Shanghai Jiao Tong University]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Ramon Wyss is professor emeritus in theoretical nuclear physics at KTH the Royal Institute of Technology. |url=https://ins.sjtu.edu.cn/seminars/2409 |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=ins.sjtu.edu.cn}}</ref>

In 2009, he was reappointed Vice-President for international projects at KTH.<ref name=":1" />

'''Research and Opinions'''

Wyss's theoretical contributions in [[nuclear physics]] include simplified [[Microscopic scale|microscopic]]-[[macroscopic]] approaches and [[Glossary of astronomy|rotational models]], notably in studies of backbending and high-spin band structures.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wyss |first=Ramon |date=2021-09-02 |title=Can Nuclear Physics Improve Earthquake Forecasting? |journal=Nuclear Physics News |volume=31 |issue=3 |pages=34–37 |doi=10.1080/10619127.2021.1954451 |bibcode=2021NPNew..31...34W |issn=1061-9127|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":6" />

His research has centered on [[nuclear structure]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wyss |first1=R. |last2=Nyberg |first2=J. |last3=Johnson |first3=A. |last4=Bengtsson |first4=R. |last5=Nazarewicz |first5=W. |date=1988 |title=Highly deformed intruder bands in the A≈130 mass region |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0370269388914220 |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en |volume=215 |issue=2 |pages=211–217 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(88)91422-0|bibcode=1988PhLB..215..211W |url-access=subscription }}</ref>, including [[rotational motion]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wyss |first1=R. |last2=Satuła |first2=W. |date=1995-06-01 |title=Blocking effects at super-deformed shape |url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693%2895%2900439-R |journal=Physics Letters B |volume=351 |issue=4 |pages=393–399 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(95)00439-R |bibcode=1995PhLB..351..393W |issn=0370-2693|url-access=subscription }}</ref>, backbending phenomena, [[particle decay]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Qi |first1=C. |last2=Xu |first2=F. R. |last3=Liotta |first3=R. J. |last4=Wyss |first4=R. |date=2009-08-13 |title=Universal Decay Law in Charged-Particle Emission and Exotic Cluster Radioactivity |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.103.072501 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=103 |issue=7 |article-number=072501 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.103.072501 |pmid=19792636 |issn=0031-9007|arxiv=0909.4492 |bibcode=2009PhRvL.103g2501Q }}</ref> and the development of nuclear models linking experimental and theoretical approaches.

He co-authored research on [[Neutron–proton ratio|neutron-proton]] pairing in [[Atomic nucleus|nuclei]] and other mass systematics, reinforcing the effectiveness of accessible models in describing complex nuclear behaviors.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wyss |first1=Ramon A. |last2=Davies |first2=Paul John |last3=Satuła |first3=Wojciech |last4=Wadsworth |first4=Robert |date=2007-07-02 |title=Contrasting behavior in the rotational structure of the ''T<sub>Z</sub>''=1/2 nuclei <sup>73</sup>Kr and <sup>75</sup>Rb: A possible fingerprint of ''T''=0 neutron-proton pairing correlations |journal=Physical Review C |volume=76 |issue=1 |article-number=011301 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.76.011301}}</ref>

In Sweden, he engaged in the debate for nuclear power as an energy source reducing [[CO2 emission]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-01-27 |title=DN Debatt. "Tio råd till den som vill bygga ny kärnkraft i Sverige" |url=https://www.dn.se/debatt/tio-rad-till-den-som-vill-bygga-ny-karnkraft-i-sverige/ |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=[[Dagens Nyheter]] |language=sv}}</ref>
